nodes.label: v3/CONSTANTS.md — the constants and tunables inventory for v3/: 313 rows, each naming the file and symbol, what the value controls, and a provenance class (unknown 161, derived 115, borrowed 21, user-specified 11, swept 5). unknown means no evidence for the value was found anywhere. check_constants.py parses the table and re-reads each named symbol out of the source with ast; v3/test_constants_inventory.py fails the suite on drift.

What the inventory covers: every hard-coded constant and tunable in v3/ — module-level constants, environment-variable defaults (name and default recorded), and numeric or string literals acting as a threshold, limit, cap, k, temperature, batch size, timeout, tolerance, seed, model id, prompt or dimension, including ones in function signature defaults, inline in expressions, and inside Cypher strings. Trivially structural literals (0/1 as index or identity, list indices, obvious loop bounds, message-truncation slices in error strings) are out, as are the test files (v3/test_*.py, v3/artefact/tests/), which set no runtime behaviour.

unknown is the point of the provenance column: no evidence for the value was found anywhere — not in the user's turns, not in a design doc, not in a git message, not in a sweep, not in the code's own comments. It is not a judgement that the value is wrong, and it is never a guess dressed up as a reason. A rationale written in a comment after the fact is not evidence of derivation and is recorded as unknown with the comment quoted. A reason that restates the value's effect ("a missing weight contributes nothing") is unknown, as is a name the code invents for its own artefact: a cache directory, a lock file, a manifest label. Where a rule's shape follows from something real but its number does not — a numerical guard's magnitude, a rounding precision, a budget sized with headroom, MAX_DEGRADED_RETRIES, the empty-content retry, the routing clamp's 2× ceiling — the row is unknown and states both halves, because the number is the thing being asked about.

derived is the strict class: the value is forced by something outside the choice — a name the code or the dataset already carries, a schema or a library's requirement, an arithmetic identity, or a decision with a citation. "Outside" excludes the code's own prose: a comment, a docstring or a help string is written by whoever wrote the value, so it can describe a derivation but can never be one. The citation has to reach something that exists independently of this repo's source — the dataset's own file shape, a vendor's published limit, a library's contract, a paper or dataset card, a user turn, a design doc, or a measurement in a run folder. A path that points at content another stage writes stays derived: the two must agree.

The where column names the file and the symbol, never a line number. Two backticked parts — file · SYMBOL — is a module-level assignment. Three — file · scope · literal — is a literal with no symbol of its own, located by its enclosing function (or by the Cypher constant it sits inside) and quoted. check_constants.py at the repo root parses this table, re-reads each named symbol out of the source with ast, and compares the recorded value against the code's.

Across the 20 numeric tunables and flags of artefact_v1.py — W_TAG, W_DESC, W_SCOPE, STR_FACET, STR_WCHUNK, STR_RELEVANCE, STR_DESC_HINT, STR_SCOPE_MATCH, STR_GUIDE, K_LEVELS, GUIDE_TAU, GUIDE_C, GUIDE_M, GUIDE_LAMBDA, GUIDE_SEED, AGG, NORM, NORM_SCOPE, KNN_OVERFETCH, CURVE_WALK — git log -p --follow shows no assignment line ever removed or modified: each stands at its first-commit value. The claim covers those 20 lines and nothing else; model ids in particular are outside it (INTERPRET_MODEL has carried three values).

The 2026-07-23 combine sweep and the 2026-08 weight sweeps ran around the defaults without changing any of them, and where a sweep produced a winner it was not adopted: HERB_NORM_SCOPE sweeps global at 0.6812 while per_path at 0.6039 ships. So almost nothing in the artefact arm qualifies as swept under the definition "the value was selected by a sweep" — the sweeps are evidence about the values, not evidence for them, and the rows say so.

No row marked swept names a run folder that is still on disk. Those folders were retrieval-only, were not retained, and — checked against git log --all --diff-filter=A — were never committed either, so they are unrecoverable rather than merely deleted. Each such row opens with "evidence not retained" and states the figure as unsupported, because the only surviving record of it is v3/output/DATA_README.md, a sibling document in the same shipment, and a sibling document is not evidence. Citing one here and having it cite back is circular, so no row rests its class on DATA_README.md or docs/ENVIRONMENT.md: a figure either points at a run folder, a code line, a user turn or a dated state doc, or it is marked unsupported in place. CURVE_WALK and NORM_SCOPE are the two cases where a surviving folder does carry the reading.
Evidence keys used by the rows: turns:L<n> = docs/canon/raw/user_turns_all.md; state:<file> = the flat state-transfer folder under OneDrive; canon:<file> = docs/canon/.

Counts, recounted from the table by python check_constants.py --counts, which reads the rows back and tallies them so the classes sum to the total. Total rows 313: unknown 161, derived 115, borrowed 21, user-specified 11, swept 5. python check_constants.py re-reads 176 of those rows against the source — 152 with a value the parser can compare on both sides, 24 where the symbol is verified but the value is prose or an expression it will not evaluate; the remaining 137 name no module-level symbol and are reported UNCHECKED. The tie-break, stated because three rows need one: a provenance cell may name two classes when a row's shape is forced but its wording or its number is not — the tagger SYSTEM, the interpreter SYSTEM and _EXCLUDE_RE each open derived and close unknown — and such a row is tallied as unknown, the weaker class winning because a row is only as supported as its least supported half. check_constants.provenance_of scans the fixed order unknown → derived → borrowed → user-specified → swept and returns the first class present, so unknown takes any row that mentions it; reading the leading bold token instead would move those three rows and print 157 / 118. v3/test_constants_inventory.py holds the counts to the table.

Two rows carry a disagreement between sources and say so in place: NIM_SECONDS_BETWEEN_CALLS, where the 3.0 s default and the comment beside it describe different rates, and HERB_NORM_SCOPE, where the sweep measures a different winner than the value that ships. Three rows describe _check_judge_context_budget, a function no call site invokes: MAX_JUDGE_CONTEXT_CHARS, _CONTEXT_HEAVY_LLM and the [:8] report cut.

What binds the artefact arm to its graph, all user-specified or derived. DATABASE / NEO4J_DATABASE = "herb-eval": which Neo4j DB every artefact number comes from — the session in prepare_over_corpus and answer_one_question, the det leg's per-database product vocabulary, and one half of the cluster-guide cache-entry name built by _guide_key, so pointing the arm at another database also reads a different guide entry; user-specified, "i want to retrieve the old 'post thesis cleaned up v1 graph', the one using 'herb-eval' db, and run the the current v3 arm and eval at k=50 on that one" (turns:L344). DATASET_ID = "Salesforce__HERB", the Source.name the v1 build wrote, filtering every File match. RUN_ID = "pilot_full_herb", the single run_id present in herb-eval, deciding which tagging run's HAS_TAG edges are visible and naming the other half of the guide cache entry. ALL_FACETS = (topic, entities, activity, temporal, evidence) — borrowed from the facet set baked into herb-eval's HAS_TAG.facets, and the canonical axis order of everything keyed by facet; it is folded into _INTERP_SIG, so editing it invalidates every cached plan. GROUND_INDEX = tag_emb and DESC_INDEX = chunk_desc_emb are the two vector indexes reembed_herb_eval creates and prepare requires present.

K_LEVELS = (8, 16, 32, 64) — the doubling level sequence in _multi_k_support; the tag-pool width and both description-pool widths (K_LEVELS[-1] = 64); the extension base for stated scope; _n_levels's multiplicity; the level count in _ABS_REF; the sufficiency review's evidence ladder; and the knn_levels field of the retrieval meta. Provenance unknown, and named by the user as exactly the problem: "arbitrarily decided hard limits, like the 64 chunk limit, i bet there is way more than 1 of these dumb limits lying around not beeing seen" (turns:L4217; the 64 is K_LEVELS[-1]). canon:OPEN_DECISIONS.md §15 and canon:USER_CANON.md Part IV.C both list it as underived. Measured consequence: "the distance term spans 1.41× while the level staircase spans 4× → K_LEVELS is the value model, not a budget" (state:2026-08-02-corpus-facts.md). _ABS_UNIT = 4.0 is derived as 1 / _ABS_REF_DIST ** 2 and _ABS_REF = 16.0 as len(K_LEVELS) * _ABS_UNIT, so it inherits K_LEVELS's unknown provenance. KNN_OVERFETCH = 4 over-fetches both vector indexes at all three kNN call sites; its stated purpose of giving the row filters headroom is measured vacuous — filter survival is exactly 1.0 on both indexes and Chunk.empty exists on 0 chunks.

The cross-path combine weights, all unknown. W_TAG = 1.0 weights the tag path in the cross-path sum and the tag term of the door trace; it was swept at 0 / 0.5 / 2 / 4 (WTAG0, WTAG05, WTAG2, WTAG4, WG_WTAG0, WG_WTAG2 on gold100, none on disk) and the sweep did not select 1.0. The HERB_W_TAG=0 result is unsupported: neither record carrying it is primary — state:2026-08-02-benchmark-validity-record.md says "+0.027, t 2.56" against a Westfall–Young bar of +0.036, while v3/output/DATA_README.md, a sibling document, gives +0.0062, CI [−0.0040, +0.0165], W/L/T 4/2/94. They cannot both be right: 6 nonzero deltas summing to a mean of +0.027 force t ≤ 2.514, so the state doc's pair is internally impossible, and settling it needs a fresh retrieval-only run at HERB_W_TAG=0. W_DESC = 1.0 (description path) and W_SCOPE = 1.0 (stated-scope path) were never varied in any run manifest under v3/output/.

The modifier strengths on the tag path, lerped through _mod. STR_FACET = 0.0 (edge facet-agreement) is swept with evidence not retained and the figure unsupported: artefact_v1_haikuFACET__gold100__20260723T151010Z is absent from disk and was never committed, and its reading (0.6129, +0.0090, CI [−0.0167, +0.0346]) survives only in v3/output/DATA_README.md, as does the judgement that "facets are null" overstates a bounded failure to detect (±0.035) with a weakly positive tendency. STR_WCHUNK = 1.0, STR_RELEVANCE = 1.0, STR_DESC_HINT = 1.0 and STR_SCOPE_MATCH = 1.0 are unknown and were never varied in any manifest. STR_RELEVANCE is flagged as an open contamination channel: relevance_to_file "was produced by a v1 LLM stage whose prompt contained the answer key … never ablated"; 22 run_manifest.json files remain on disk, 5 carry HERB_STR_RELEVANCE, all at 1.0. STR_GUIDE = 0.0 turns the cluster-guide lift off entirely — no cache load, no guide_stats, no guide meta block — and values below 0 fail loud at import; its swept figures rest on folders that are neither on disk nor in any commit.

DESC_HINT_M = 2.0 is the factor a scope-hint-matching description chunk carries into the description path's modifier, lerped by STR_DESC_HINT. Nothing derives 2.0; it is exposed as an env coefficient and recorded in RETRIEVAL_FLAGS, so a run's manifest carries the value it ran under, and state:2026-08-02-benchmark-validity-record.md names it as one of three values whose origin "cannot be closed". DESC_HINT_M and DESC_CUT are younger tunables and sit outside the first-commit-value claim: DESC_HINT_M was added by bb95e4b (2026-08-05, "tags route and weight, never exclude"), the only commit that has ever touched its assignment line. Being younger than the runs, both are in none of them — RETRIEVAL_FLAGS carries HERB_DESC_HINT_M and HERB_DESC_CUT (23 entries, 24 on the det leg) but no run_manifest.json under v3/output/ records either, so every figure quoted in the inventory was produced under a flag schema that differs from today's, and neither the value 2.0 nor the description cut has been varied or measured.

DESC_CUT / HERB_DESC_CUT ships on and decides what the flat regime's description lookup admits. On: the anchor chunk's containing cluster out of _desc_area's dendrogram chain (_anchor_cluster — the first merge, since level 0 is the anchor alone), so the neighborhood's own geometry sets the width and the kNN trim is only the ceiling. Off: the whole K_LEVELS[-1]-wide neighborhood. Chunks outside the admitted cluster enter neither the union pool nor the description base, and the admitted count is the chunks field of the walk entry. Provenance unknown — the user names the fixed width as the defect (turns:L4217, the 64 being K_LEVELS[-1]) but no turn names a replacement rule: cutting at the anchor's first merge is the code's own choice, and so is shipping it on. It is younger than every run under v3/output/, so no manifest carries it and no measurement separates the two settings.

The regime switches. CURVE_WALK / HERB_CURVE_WALK defaults off and selects the progressive-frontier walk over the flat regime, also switching the kept_k rule and the curve_walk meta block. Its flag-isolated pair is on disk and gold-100 n=100, budget-matched at 478.0 vs 480.9 ids: artefact_v1_clusterKglob__gold100__20260723T170853Z and JUDGE_artefactGlobal__gold100__20260723T170605Z differ in HERB_CURVE_WALK alone (true vs false), all 15 other entries identical — 0.7492 on against 0.6812 off, +0.0680, CI [+0.0306, +0.1053], sign-flip p 2.45e-4. The on leg carries no eval_results.jsonl so its 0.7492 is recomputed from arm_outputs.jsonl; the off leg's stored 0.6812 cell lives in its re-judge sibling JUDGE_artefactGlobal__gold100__20260723T170605Z__j-claude-haiku-4-5/eval_results.jsonl. Isolating the flag is not isolating a mechanism: it switches the stop rule, clusters the description path, and changes the kept_k rule together. DOOR_TRACE (per-chunk path-value trace into meta.door_trace, observability only, heavy), FRESH_INTERP (re-run the interpreter vs read the cached plan) and NO_REVIEW (disable the sufficiency cut) all default off with the rationale being the comment's own. RETRIEVAL_FLAGS is the 23-entry list the runner copies into run_manifest.json, one entry per exposed env knob so a run documents its own value model; the det leg extends it with HERB_DET_FACETS.

Per-query K did not bind in the one surviving CURVE_WALK run: meta.curve_walk.kept is 50 on 100/100 questions and semantic has a minimum of 122, so kept_k = min(len(semantic), k) took the caller's k every time. The stop rule fired on all 100 (stopped true, 7–146 levels opened) and never reached the depth. That delta is ordering and membership; per-query K has never been measured on gold-100. The stop rule itself is _gap_break, whose three-gap minimum history, 1e-9 float-noise floor and mean + 2.0 × std threshold are each unknown and inert at the default.

How the paths fold and scale. AGG = "sum" decides how a path folds a chunk's support over the parts that vouch for it; an unknown value fails loud at import. Its max alternatives were swept with evidence not retained: haikuMAX and haikuMAXABS are absent from disk and were never committed, and detMAX__gold100__probe survives only as a 249-byte terminal log recording "100/100 answered, 0 failed" with neither a recall figure nor a flag value. NORM = "relative" scales each path's base reaches before the weighted sum, also fail-loud on an unknown value; haikuABS and haikuNONE are absent, detABS and detNONE survive only as 249- and 251-byte terminal logs. NORM_SCOPE = "per_path" chooses min-max per path over min-max globally across the union, inert unless NORM is relative — and the measurement contradicts the shipped value on both legs: global reads 0.6812 against per_path 0.6039 on the model leg, and artefact_v1_detGLOB__gold100__probe, on disk, reads 0.7394 against the det default's 0.7339, +0.0055, CI [+0.0004, +0.0106], the one det-leg sweep delta whose CI excludes zero. That folder carries no eval_results.jsonl, so the 0.7394 is recomputed from arm_outputs.jsonl. No record explains keeping per_path.

The cluster-guide constants, all unknown. GUIDE_TAU = 0.01 is the membership-cell floor, cells below it dropping before the guidance mass is summed; canon:CONTRADICTION_MAP.md §2 cites it by name as one of the arm's unbased constants. GUIDE_C = 128 is the number of k-means prototypes per facet and names the cache entry. GUIDE_M = 1.5 is the fuzzifier of the membership exponent, with values at or below 1.0 failing loud at import — the > 1.0 guard is derived because the exponent divides by m − 1, but 1.5 itself has no record. GUIDE_LAMBDA = 0.05 is the participation floor λ in ω̃ = λ + (1−λ)·ω, applied by build_tag_clusters.floor_participation. GUIDE_SEED = 20260731 is the k-means++ seed and the digits are the build date, not a property of the data. GUIDE_CACHE_DIR = output/tag_cluster_cache is read by the arm and written by build_tag_clusters.py, which imports the constant rather than agreeing with it independently.

The interpreter's model-facing constants. INTERPRET_MODEL = "claude-haiku-4-5" drives both interpreter passes and the sufficiency review and is part of the interpretation cache key; unknown, because the user names haiku for the Claude lane (turns:L1186) and for the evals (turns:L3820) and is aware the arm makes haiku calls (turns:L2865), but no turn names a model for the interpreter, and git shows three values with no rationale in any commit message. _PASS1_SYSTEM (description, tags, gate — interpolating OFFERED_SECTIONS), _PASS2_SYSTEM (the per-tag facet score array on a declared 0.0–1.0 scale) and _REVIEW_SYSTEM (the {"sufficient": bool} contract) are all agent-written prose with no record deriving the wording. _INTERP_SIG is derived: a sha256 over the two prompts, FILLER, ALL_FACETS and five function sources, so a cached plan may only be served by the interpreter that would produce it now. FILLER (data, information, content, record, text, chunk, item, find) drops generic interpreter tags before the parts are formed; it has no derivation from the corpus, and "find" is named in state:2026-08-02-benchmark-validity-record.md as one of five terms whose presence shows the question file was open when it was written. Pass-1 max_tokens 512, pass-2 1024, review 128, the 0.2 neutral facet value, the two-try attempt loop and the 480.0 s NIM timeout are unknown; temperature 0 and the [0.0, 1.0] facet clamp are derived.

The section enums, all derived. GATE_SECTIONS is the full nine-name top-level section enum of a HERB product file, oracle sections included; its one read site is OFFERED_SECTIONS, which subtracts EXCLUDED_SECTIONS, so the interpreter is offered the subset and never the tuple. EXCLUDED_SECTIONS = (answerable_questions, unanswerable_questions, product_profile) are the sections retrieval can never return — the eval oracle, the same strip artefact/derive_corpus.py · ORACLE_KEYS performs plus product_profile. _EXCLUDED_PARAM is the list form bound as $excludedSections in all four Cyphers because the Neo4j driver takes a list, not a tuple. OFFERED_SECTIONS is the six names named inside the pass-1 prompt, the whitelist _parse_gate validates against, and the vocabulary the det leg matches literally.

_tag_affinity's lift, support × (1 + affinity) in _part_levels, multiplies tag support before the anchor argmax; affinity is a fraction in [0, 1], so the ceiling is 2×. Unknown, and recorded as an unflagged up-to-2× with no HERB_STR_* exposure and no manifest entry: "_tag_affinity is an unflagged ×2 applied before the anchor argmax — changes membership, no STR_*, in no manifest" (state:2026-08-02-corpus-facts.md). The Cypher null defaults sit beside it: coalesce(r.w_chunk, 0.0) is unknown because a null reads as 0.0 and _mod collapses that chunk's whole tag score to zero where 1.0, the neutral factor, is equally available; coalesce(r.w_facets[fi], 0.0) and the unknown-facet ELSE 0.0 are unknown for the same reason; coalesce(c.relevance_to_file, 1.0), coalesce(c.empty, false), coalesce(c.section, ""), coalesce(r.facets, []) and coalesce(c.years, []) are derived.

pipelines/artefact_v1_det.py — the deterministic leg. INTERPRET_MODEL = "deterministic" is a manifest label, not a model. _EID (\beid_[0-9a-f]+\b) and _YEAR (\b(?:19|20)\d{2}\b) are derived from HERB's own id and year forms. _FACET_MODE / HERB_DET_FACETS defaults to "" and selects which of the support / routing / edges facet placements run, also naming the facet_channel meta field; the folders that would attribute it (detf, detA, detE, detR on gold100, 2026-07-21) are absent from disk and were never committed, and the one surviving folder of that family, artefact_v1_detK__gold100__20260721T230502Z, carries "retrieval_flags": null — the key present and empty — so no HERB_DET_FACETS value was recorded in that era at all. FACETS_ON, ROUTING_ON and EDGES_ON are derived, each reading _FACET_MODE. _ANCHOR_TEXTS (five facet-meaning sentences) and _FACET_WORDS (four keyword lists) are agent-written prose; state:2026-08-02-benchmark-validity-record.md names "reviewers"/"authors" in the live _FACET_WORDS among five terms whose presence shows the question file was open. The 0.2 neutral facet floor and plan neutral vector are unknown, the 1.0 triggered weight derived. The routing disagreement clamp [0.0, 1.0] never binds: disagreement is bounded by the sum of the question direction's two largest facet weights, at most 0.769231 over the 16 trigger patterns, so the attainable stretch ceiling is 1.7692×.

The one unenforced invariant — a relationship between constants the code depends on and nothing checks. _ANCHOR_TEXTS's keys must be ALL_FACETS, in the same order (pipelines/artefact_v1_det.py · _ANCHOR_TEXTS against pipelines/artefact_v1.py · ALL_FACETS). _anchors() embeds _ANCHOR_TEXTS.values() as the rows of the anchor matrix; _facet_direction() builds the question's trigger vector by iterating _ANCHOR_TEXTS's keys and looking each name up in a dict _facet_triggers() built from ALL_FACETS. So the support shaper's G @ qdir and the router's (gap * qdir) pair anchor row i with trigger weight i only while the two sequences agree. A facet in ALL_FACETS and absent from _ANCHOR_TEXTS drops silently out of every direction vector while _FACET_WORDS can still fire its trigger; a key in _ANCHOR_TEXTS and absent from ALL_FACETS raises KeyError at the first det question. Nothing asserts the equality, no test covers it, and no comment mentions it.

The shared top-k budget, the inventory's clearest user-specified rows. orchestrator.DEFAULT_TOP_K = 50 is k for every arm on every run and run.py's -k default reads it: "so, for academic rigor, we have done k=50 now.. should we do more k's ?" (turns:L217), and he runs -k 50 himself (turns:L394, :3719). His later ruling limits how it may be read: "k=50 does not mean the same for all arms, and thats retarded" (turns:L2901). answer_one_question's k: int = 50 default in both artefact_v1.py and artefact_v1_det.py carries the same citation, as does model_test.py's -k. truncate_k.py's --ks default 5,10,15,20,30,40,50 is user-specified too: "so not 5,10,15,20,30,40 ?" (turns:L221), immediately after accepting k=50. The three baseline arms' DEFAULT_TOP_K = 10 are unknown and dead in practice, overridden by orchestrator.DEFAULT_TOP_K; the user attacked a 10: "2. 10? fucking why just 10?" (turns:L730).

pipelines/lucene.py — the sparse baseline, mostly borrowed. K1 = 0.9 and B = 0.4 are the BM25 term-frequency saturation and length normalization from "Resources for Brewing BEIR" (Kamalloo et al. 2023) reference defaults, cited in the module docstring. method="lucene" is the Apache Lucene / Elasticsearch / Anserini variant and bm25s's own default; the English Snowball/Porter2 stemmer and the "en" stopword list are bm25s's own analysis chain, which the docstring is explicit approximates rather than reproduces Lucene's EnglishAnalyzer; the indexed text is title + "\n" + contents, the standard BEIR concatenation. ARTIFACT_TYPES is derived from the dataset's own file shape: a raw HERB products/*.json carries exactly ten top-level keys and this tuple is the six left after derive_corpus.STRIP_KEYS removes four, verified against data/raw/Salesforce__HERB/products/.

pipelines/vector.py — the dense baseline. EMBED_MODEL = "nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2" is the one embedder across every arm: this arm's corpus and query sides, the artefact arm's query embeds and cache key, the graph's semantic layer via reembed_herb_eval.py, the tag matrix via embed_tags.py, and RAGAS. User-specified: "just fucking make a new graph with the nemo embedder instead and delete the old embeddings in it" (turns:L438); "The things that were embedded before should be embedded with nemotron now, that was fucking all you had to do" (turns:L572). EMBED_BATCH = 2048 is derived — NVIDIA's published hosted /embeddings limit of 2048 inputs per request, so batching to it is the maximum legal batch rather than a chosen size. The 8192-token context claim is borrowed from the nemotron model card and is why artifacts embed whole with no chunking. QUERY_VECS_PATH and ARTIFACT_TYPES are derived; truncate="NONE", CACHE_DIR and the [:16] cache-key digest length are unknown.

pipelines/hybrid.py — the late-fusion baseline. ALPHA / HERB_HYBRID_ALPHA = 0.5 is the fusion weight on the dense arm and this arm's one manifest flag; the ends are measured (hybA0_lucene__gold100__20260723T154130Z at 0.0, hybA1_vector at 1.0, hybrid__gold100__20260723T153637Z at 0.5) but no record selects 0.5 — it is the even blend by construction. OVERFETCH = 4 is each arm's fetch depth as a multiple of k before the fusion, the same numeral as artefact_v1.KNN_OVERFETCH with no record connecting or deriving either. The alpha range check [0.0, 1.0], loud at import, is derived: the fusion is a convex combination.

pipelines/artefact.py — the v3-native arm entry. DEFAULT_TOP_K = 10 is unknown and this arm appears in 0 of 121 run manifests. PRODUCT_LITERAL_BOOST = 1.0 is an additive lift on every chunk in a named product's file; the comment offers a rationale ("roughly one strong facet-phrase match") with no measurement, and ablate_boost.py was built to attribute it with its result recorded nowhere. TODAY = "2026-06-28" is a frozen build date hard-coded as the run's today, the reference date relative phrases resolve against. _KEY_PATH and the stable argsort tiebreak are derived.

artefact/ — the native rebuild stages. CAP_TOKENS = 3000 is the chunk size cap every kind packs toward and is the best-documented constant in the tree and still underived: recorded as a design decision (canon:USER_CANON.md:1431, 06-03/04, [DOC] not a user turn) explicitly framed "a calibration seed, not a verdict" with a named §15 sweep that was never run (canon:OPEN_DECISIONS.md §14), and no turn in the record names 3000. GAP_FACTOR = 6 breaks an episode when a gap exceeds 6× the channel's median positive gap; the comment claims the §15 sweep firms it and that sweep does not exist. LONG_TEXT_CHARS = 200 is a dispatch threshold on real data with no measurement behind it. TAGGER_MODEL = "z-ai/glm-5.1" is unknown — "Why the built tagger is z-ai/glm-5.1 when the documented choice was Mistral Large — 06-28 — Undocumented" (canon:USER_CANON.md Part IV.E). INTERPRETER_MODEL = "meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct" has no record selecting it. DB = "herb-v3" is unknown: distinct-from-herb-eval is forced, herb-v3 is not, and the database was never materialized. tag_id = "{chunk_id}#{position}" is derived from design §7 and measured a regression — it destroys "the 6,792 shared-phrase tags that are the only Chunk → Tag ← Chunk path". file_id = sha256[:24] is unknown, and newline translation on Windows changes the hash, so "re-deriving the corpus invalidates all 5,377 chunk_ids and the tag checkpoint". ORACLE_KEYS, RAG_UNSAFE_KEYS and STRIP_KEYS are derived from HERB's own key names and the dataset card's RAG Evaluation Note; the tagger's 40 RPM projection rate is derived from NVIDIA's published per-account NIM rate limit.

orchestrator.py — the run engine and the shared generator. DEFAULT_CORPUS = data/corpus/Salesforce__HERB is the only data a pipeline sees, derived as the oracle-stripped corpus view. GENERATOR_MODEL = "qwen/qwen3.5-397b-a17b" is the one answer-writer injected into every arm unless --generator overrides it; unknown — no turn selects it, and the user's turns about it are complaints ("why the fuck are we even using qwen anymore, this is so stupid", turns:L1380; "qwen ia NIM is fucking uselessly slow", turns:L1328), with git showing a mistral predecessor and no rationale in either commit. _ANSWER_SCHEMA is derived — the answer is the only thing the generator owns. temperature 0 is derived for determinism; enable_thinking False, max_tokens 8192, min_tokens 1 and the 480.0 s timeout are unknown, each resting on the comment's own rationale. DEFAULT_WORKERS = 2 is unknown and run.py overrides it to 1; MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 10 is unknown.

run.py — the CLI. ARMS (6 arm names) is derived from the modules under pipelines/. The gold and 10smoke id-set files are derived as the named fixed sets — data/gold100.jsonl is not the file build_question_sets.py writes (state:2026-08-02-benchmark-validity-record.md records 6/100 overlap). The rejudge worker auto-size len(ids) × len(metrics_to_run()) is derived because the shared judge pool JUDGE_INFLIGHT is the real cap, and the wide-parallel judge families (claude, gpt-, gemini) are derived as the subscription CLI lanes with no NIM queue. The run-id timestamp format %Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ UTC and the judge slug pattern are derived. OUTPUT, -n default 5 and --workers default 1 are unknown: nim.py's pacer already enforces the rate cap across threads, so 1 is not the value the cap forces and nothing records why serial rather than 2 or 3.

contract.py, progress.py, run_lock.py, abort.py, questions.py, prompt_tokens.py. GENERATOR_SYSTEM ("Answer the question using only the provided documents. Be concise.") is the shared generator's system prompt, identical across arms — the fairness property is designed, the wording has no record. progress.py's tqdm ascii=True, dynamic_ncols=True and disable-when-not-a-tty are derived from the target terminal and from captured logs not filling with bar frames. run_lock.py's two acquire attempts are derived (one stale-clear then one attempt); the Win32 0x1000 access flag and exit code 259 are borrowed API constants; the .run.lock filename is unknown. abort.py's 0.1 s poll interval is unknown and its q/Q keys derived. questions.py's QUESTIONS path is derived. prompt_tokens.py's _TOKENIZER_ID = "Qwen/Qwen3-8B" is unknown: the family follows GENERATOR_MODEL, the 8B checkpoint does not, and nothing records whether its tokenizer is identical to the 397B generator's.

nim.py — transport, pacing, retries. BASE_URL is NVIDIA's published endpoint. NVIDIA_API_KEY plus every NVIDIA_API_KEY_WORKER_* is the whole key pool, primary first then workers in sorted name order; pool size sets the lane count _thread_key binds threads round-robin across, so it silently controls real NIM concurrency because rate limits are per account, and this machine's v3/.env defines five. The pool size is not a constant at all — it is whatever the environment supplies, recorded in no manifest. The pacing floor 1.5 s is derived exactly: 60 / 40 = 1.5 s per call against NVIDIA's published 40 requests/min, the vendor ceiling restated as a period. SECONDS_BETWEEN_CALLS = 3.0 is unknown and the comment beside it describes a different value ("5s is ~12 calls/min, well under NIM's 40/min"). RETRYABLE_STATUS {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504} and the 2 ** attempt backoff are borrowed standards; MAX_TRIES = 6, GIVE_UP_AFTER_S = 300.0, MAX_DEGRADED_RETRIES = 2, the 120.0 s default timeout and the 3.0 s DEGRADED delay are unknown. The _CLAUDE_EXE fallback ~/.local/bin/claude.exe is a hard-coded guess at one machine's install path that surfaces only as a failed subprocess when wrong.

eval/ragas.py — the judge lane. JUDGE_BACKEND is derived, read off the judge slug at import by substring — "gemini" then "gpt-" then "claude", else nim — with the same loose match as nim.py's startswith("claude"), so an alias like haiku misses every branch and silently falls through to nim. JUDGE_MODEL = "claude-haiku-4-5" is user-specified: "try haiku first then, and we can do this headless in the same way?" (turns:L1186); "we decided to use haiku for the fucking evals also" (turns:L3820); "using, as the others.. headless claude cli with my subscription" (turns:L3824). EMBED_MODEL is the same nemotron embedder, user-specified at turns:L438 and :L572. The four judge profiles (claude 64/120.0/2, gpt 64/180.0/2, gemini 64/180.0/2, giant-NIM 8/480.0/3, small-NIM 8/90.0/3) are unknown — the comments explain running wide or respecting the queue, not the numbers. RunConfig(max_retries=1) is derived from an observed failure: RAGAS's default 10× nested on nim.post's retries "turned one 429 into minutes of dead retries and, under concurrency, starved the shared pacer so parallel ran slower than serial". MAX_JUDGE_CONTEXT_CHARS = 60000 and its [:8] report cut sit inside _check_judge_context_budget, which no call site invokes.

eval/ragas_catalog.py. CATALOG holds 37 metrics, 28 of them feedable by HERB (applies=True) and 9 kept visible but unselectable — derived from the library's metric list, each row's judge / embed / needs read off the RAGAS docs. SELECTED is the 14 metrics a run actually scores: 4 free retrieval, 7 free answer-vs-gold, 3 judged. It is unknown — the free/judged split follows each metric's own cost and context_precision_llm_ref is commented out as the slow per-context pass, but nothing records why these 14 of the 28 feedable metrics, and state:2026-08-02-benchmark-validity-record.md records the consequence: "No rank-aware metric is in eval/ragas_catalog.py. Ordering changes are invisible". The ragas==0.4.3 pin is derived: the legacy ragas.metrics classes carry the id-based and non-LLM context metrics the newer collections API drops, and judged scores are not comparable across ragas versions.

Top-level scripts. build_question_sets.py's GOLD_N = 100 and GOLD_SEED = 0 are unknown, and the shipped data/gold100.jsonl is not reproducible from this script (6/100 overlap), so the constants do not describe the set in use; the equal-allocation round-robin draw is argued only by its own docstring. reembed_herb_eval.py's BACKUP_DATABASE = "herb-eval-backup" is the read-only source of chunk-description text, LEGACY_FACET_INDEXES and LEGACY_FACET_PROPS name what the superseded build wrote, and the 'cosine' vector-index similarity is the embedder's own metric on unit-normalised vectors — the metric every kNN in the arm scores under. build_tag_clusters.py's MAX_ITER = 60, TOL = 1e-7 and the 1e-6 membership distance floor are unknown; _FACET_COL is ALL_FACETS's order enumerated. compare_arms.py's DIR_RE is unknown and does not match the run-folder naming scheme it exists to read: "[a-z]+ matches neither artefact_v1 nor artefact_v1_det. The cross-arm table printer has never displayed the artefact" (state:2026-08-02-corpus-facts.md). model_test.py's MODELS is user-specified (turns:L929); ablate_boost.py's K = 10 is a one-off experiment constant whose ablation result is recorded nowhere.
